items.original_title: FinancialJuice: MUFG on FOMC

evidence.headline: FinancialJuice: MUFG on FOMC
evidence.snippet: The FOMC is very likely to remain on hold but the OIS indicates close to 10% probability of a hike. A hold would likely be accompanied by a statement similar to the statement in September when the FOMC hiked underlining the fact that the economy remains resilient. There is a risk that there could be some dissents and that would certainly be one signal of the leaning and would strengthen the market’s conviction of a hike in December. A December hike is close to fully priced. If the press conference is similar in tone to previous public engagements by Chair Warsh he is likely to come across as hawkish. We certainly don't expect anything explicit in regard to a policy decision in December but we can expect Warsh to emphasise the determination of the FOMC to meet its price stability objective.

items.original_title: FinancialJuice: JPMorgan's Feroli on FOMC

evidence.headline: FinancialJuice: JPMorgan's Feroli on FOMC
evidence.snippet: He expects the Fed to hold this week, with two hawkish dissents from Hammack and Logan (he sees a risk that Kashkari also dissents). He expects the post-meeting statement will say that “policy will deliver a timely return to price stability.” Feroli On The Press Conf: Chair Warsh will have to explain why the committee hiked after a two-tenths core PCE print in September but is now holding after an expected three-tenths outturn. Disallowing follow-up questions won't resolve the challenge. We believe the various Fed speakers cited earlier provide a reasonable blueprint for what to say: the Committee is biased to hike but wants to take more time to observe how last month's hike has affected the economy. Conveying a bias to hike, something Warsh's role model Greenspan regularly did, is a form of forward guidance, and so it may be difficult for the chair to get this across. However, one can hope there is some on-the-job learning going on. A decision to leave rates unchanged less than a week before the midterm elections that goes unexplained would only encourage thoughts that policy is being driven by considerations other than employment and inflation. ”

items.original_title: FinancialJuice: JPMorgan Analyst's Review of Markets

evidence.headline: FinancialJuice: JPMorgan Analyst's Review of Markets
evidence.snippet: I am finding this market tricky to read here and whilst plenty ol issues seemingly we have reached a reasonable level of pessimism. I have no real edge on whether tech stocks have seen the bottom but whilst energy prices remain high there is seemingly some movement on the negotiation front, but into the Midterms I just don't feel massively comfortable trusting much. The Greenback moving a touch higher yesterday, confidence data and labour market differential within were strong. Fed tonight where Warsh “should" have to sound hawkish given the recent inflation readings (not exactly new news!) and month end corporate dollar demand were explanations banded around. I do think the flow argument is pervasive so will be interesting if continues at the back end of the week. On the Fed. with the first of Warsh's task forces presenting next month I don't see him sounding extreme in his hawkishness and maybe the most market moving factor will be how many dissents there might be if the decision is in fact on hold. Plenty going on elsewhere from today, BOC will be interesting given the read through from the surprise hold from the RBNZ meeting last night but personally don't see them backing off, the UK budget where the market will be squinting for signs of negativity given the recent sterling outperformance but if can navigate a smooth enough path likely a green light for continuation, all before the ECB tomorrow and BOJ on Friday. Crosses have helped to cushion the blow of the yen's inability to hold against the dollar, last night the turn of the kiwi leg! I didn't expect a hold but will take the W and squared up especially with the upcoming election more of a hit and run, having taken euros back yesterday just leaves me short usdjpy again at better levels and with offers galor

evidence.snippet: WSJ "미국·이스라엘, 대이란 대규모 공격 재개 준비 정황 늘어"… 텍사스서 패트리엇 추가 이스라엘행 [공부의여신 네트워크] 미국과 이스라엘이 이란을 상대로 새로운 대규모 군사 작전을 준비하고 있다는 정황이 늘고 있다고 월스트리트저널(WSJ)이 보도했다. 다만 미국 정부나 이스라엘 정부의 공식 확인은 아직 나오지 않았다. WSJ에 따르면 외교 채널과 군사 채널을 통한 양국 간 소통이 이어지고 있으며, 이는 미국과 이스라엘이 이란을 상대로 한 새로운 고강도 전투 작전을 개시할 준비를 하고 있다는 여러 정황 가운데 하나라고 전했다. WSJ는 또 이스라엘이 새로운 공격을 위한 계획과 공격 목표를 이미 마련해 둔 상태라고 보도했다. 이와 함께 미군은 이스라엘의 미사일 방어 태세를 강화하기 위해 텍사스에서 패트리엇 방공 시스템 1개 포대를 추가로 이스라엘에 보내고 있는 것으로 전해졌다. 앞서 WSJ는 미국이 여러 걸프 아랍 국가에 중간선거 이후 짧고 강도 높은 군사 작전에 대비하라고 통보했다고 보도한 바 있다. 트럼프 대통령은 텍사스 러벅 유세에서 "몇 주 뒤면 이란을 보게 될 겁니다. 괜찮다면 말입니다"라고 말했고, 이후 조인트 베이스 앤드루스 귀환 직후 취재진에게 이란 문제는 "언제 끝내고 싶은지의 문제입니다"라며 "선거를 기다린다고 그들에게 도움이 되지 않을 겁니다"라고 말했다. 작전 시점과 규모, 패트리엇 추가 배치의 구체적인 일정은 아직 확인되지 않았다.
